note: Foundations admitted 2026-07-30. An entry is proposed as a widget, ruled on by the teacher, then written here. A foundations entry carries a scale instead of an API: no states, no skeleton, no per-axis verdict. Five of the ten source notes were rulings, not scales, and were redirected out of the library - see docs/FOUNDATION-TRIAGE.md.

entries.name: radius
entries.role: the corner-rounding scale: one root token, every other step a multiple of it

scale.derived: NOT derived - does not track the root

entries.relation: concentric - inner is exactly one step smaller than outer, by nesting depth. Applies to a field inside a frame; not to a nested card surface, not to media.
forbidden: adding rounded-* via className onto a HeroUI component that bakes its radius unlayered - the utility loses to baked CSS and is silently ignored
picking a radius for a new block by eye instead of by nesting depth
entries.anchors: globals.css for --radius and --field-radius; heroui.min.css for the derived steps

entries.name: gap
entries.role: Two related spacing scales — the seam between elements (gap/SeamScale) and the inset a surface gives its own content (padding/InsetScale) — govern every gap and padding value in the app.
entries.root: --spacing: 0.25rem (4px), Tailwind v4's own default root, not overridden anywhere in globals.css. Every gap-N/p-N utility compiles to calc(var(--spacing) * N).

scale.derived: 1 x root — new rung, not in the old note
scale.use: a mark attached to its owner (icon before label)
peers in one set (chip row, two buttons)
interior of a card, house default

scale.derived: NOT current — retired 2026-07-27 even though 10x4 and 16x4 are clean multiples; still present as debt in 20 files under src/

entries.relation: Concentric by relationship, not by taste: ask in order, stop at first yes — one unit of meaning -> flush; a mark on its owner -> tight (gap only); peers in a set -> related; rows of one surface -> grouped; regions of one thing -> section; features on a page -> page. Padding shares gap's 2/3/6/8 numbers off the same root but has no tight rung.
notDerived: gap-10 (40px) and gap-16 (64px) — the old note's named exceptions (PageHeader->content, landing SectionHeading->content) still compute as clean multiples of the root (10x4, 16x4) but are explicitly excluded from SeamScale and InsetScale as of the 2026-07-27 frame-tier rebuild; using them today is a violation, not a legitimate step, despite 20 files under src/ still carrying them as unmigrated debt.
collidingTokens: none found: gap-2/related (8px) and p-2/snug (8px) coincide in raw pixel value at each matching step, but both trace to the single --spacing root — unlike radius's rounded-field/rounded-xl (two independent root tokens), gap and padding can never drift apart from each other since there is only one root to move
forbidden: off-scale gap written by hand (gap-4, gap-5, gap-7, gap-9, gap-10, gap-16) on a raw className, bypassing Stack/Cluster/Grid/Split's typed gap prop — caught by nothing when the value is a plain integer: no-fractional-spacing only matches N.5, no-arbitrary-token only matches bracket syntax (gap-[7px])
off-scale margin (m-5, mt-7…) — caught by nothing: no MarginScale type exists at all in _spacing.ts; margin relies solely on the same two regex lints

a hand-rolled <div className="flex gap-…"> instead of the typed frame component — caught by nothing; only the typed gap/padding prop of Stack/Cluster/Grid/Split turns an off-scale value into a compiler error, and a caller can always skip the frame entirely
readBy: inset (same frames' padding callers reading InsetScale)
radius (the concentric radius formula uses padding as its variable, per radius.md)

entries.name: typography
entries.role: The type-size ladder exposed by the app's own Typography atom (size prop) — selects among heading levels, body sizes, and code; governs font-size and, for headings, which weight tiers are real.
entries.root: None. Every step is an independently hand-set Tailwind font-size utility (Tailwind's own named type scale: text-xs/sm/base/lg/xl/2xl/3xl/4xl) — not a multiplier of a single custom property the way radius/gap are.

scale.use: top-level heading, baked font-semibold tracking-tight via HeroTypography.Heading level=1
level-5 heading — smallest heading the atom exposes

scale.derived: text-lg, hand-set — NEW rung, not in the old note
scale.use: body-scale option, same px as h5

scale.derived: RETIRED — no longer in the live TypographySize union; the vendor .typography--h6/body* CSS classes still exist in @heroui/styles but the atom never references them

entries.relation: No formula connects the steps — Tailwind's own named type scale, picked by role not ratio: h1-h5 are heading levels (HeroTypography.Heading, baked font-semibold tracking-tight); xs/sm/base/lg are body sizes rendered as bare text-* classes with NO leading-* override, so they fall through to Tailwind's own default line-height per size rather than HeroUI's own wider leading-7/6/5; code is its own branch.
notDerived: h6 and the old body/body-sm/body-xs names no longer exist in the live TypographySize union (only h1..h5, xs/sm/base/lg, code) — dead vendor CSS classes remain but are unreferenced.
lg (18px, body scale) is a genuinely new rung not present in the pre-2026-07-25 note, added when the size axis merged into one prop.
collidingTokens: h5 and lg both compute to text-lg (18px) today but diverge in intent and render path: h5 goes through HeroTypography.Heading level=5 (baked font-semibold tracking-tight, weight=bold is a real third tier), lg goes through the bare body branch (font-normal by default, weight=semibold folds into the same class as medium, no tracking-tight) — picking one for the other changes whether the text reads as a heading or a lead paragraph even though the glyph size is identical.
forbidden: weight passed together with isLink — caught by nothing: weight is a flat optional prop with no type conditioning on isLink, and the isLink branch never reads weight at all, so it is silently dropped with no error and no visible effect

weight="semibold" at body scale (xs/sm/base/lg or isButton) expecting a third tier distinct from weight="medium" — caught by nothing: both branches fold semibold into the same font-medium class as medium, the two are visually indistinguishable; semibold is only a real third tier on h1-h5, and there weight="bold" DOES take real visible effect (passed straight through to HeroTypography.Heading), contrary to the old note's uncertainty about whether it does anything at all
readBy: text (every body of copy routes size selection through this scale)
color (Typography's own color prop only bakes default/muted at the atom layer, per the color ruling)

entries.name: elevation
entries.role: The shadow depth a surface reads at rest vs floating; picks one of three baked HeroUI shadow tiers by role, feeding the `surface` axis's border-vs-shadow decision. Does not decide border vs shadow itself.

scale.derived: hand-set in @heroui/styles, not derived from anything — no root exists

scale.value: identical string to shadow-surface, both light and dark
scale.derived: hand-set independently; happens to match shadow-surface today, not the same token

scale.value: light: 0 2px 8px 0 #0000000f, 0 -6px 12px 0 #00000008, 0 14px 28px 0 #00000014; dark: 0 0 1px 0 #ffffff4d inset (switches to an inset highlight, not a drop shadow)
scale.use: popover / dropdown / tooltip / modal-content — the floating layer above everything else

entries.relation: Not numeric — role selection: resting content (card, field) gets the shallow tier, anything floating above the page gets the overlay tier. A riding rule follows from the dark-mode collapse: once a surface nests inside another surface, shadow goes invisible in dark mode, so the app switches to a border there instead — top-level = shadow, nested = border, never both on one layer. Top-level Card is the one committed exception, forced shadow-only since 2026-06-30 (`.card{border:none!important}`).
notDerived: No root token exists for this scale at all, so nothing technically fails to derive — the trap instead is that shadow-surface and shadow-field collapse to fully invisible in dark mode (0 0 0 0 transparent inset), which looks like it should still behave like light mode and silently does not.
forbidden: reaching for an ad-hoc shadow-[...] arbitrary value to make a block feel raised, instead of picking shadow-surface/shadow-field/shadow-overlay by role
stacking a border AND a shadow on the same nested surface to mark its edge
entries.verifiedAgainst: @heroui/styles/dist/heroui.min.css (grepped --surface-shadow / --field-shadow / --overlay-shadow, light and .dark values directly out of the minified bundle); D:/Repositories/starci-academy/src/app/globals.css (.card{border:none!important} override, grepped for 'shadow')

entries.name: breakpoints
entries.role: The viewport-width ladder Tailwind's sm:/md:/lg:/xl:/2xl: variants key off; decides which rule applies at which window width. It does not govern container-query breakpoints, which are a separate, lookalike-named ladder covered in this same entry because the collision is the real risk.

scale.derived: Tailwind default, not derived from any app root
scale.use: the mobile/desktop cut most rules key off (hide/show tab labels, input variant by surface)
rarely load-bearing alone — the zone between mobile and lg
the rail/2-pane opening boundary, for anything living OUTSIDE the app shell

entries.relation: Each step is an independent Tailwind default; no formula connects them. The relation that matters is between THREE parallel scales sharing lookalike names and, in one case, the same numbers: viewport (sm:), the app's own shell-container scale (@app-sm:, pinned to the same px values, for anything living inside the narrowable shell column), and Tailwind's own built-in local-container scale (@sm:, a genuinely different, smaller px value, used validly elsewhere for grids sizing off their own immediate wrapper). Which one applies depends on where the element renders, not on which name looks right.
notDerived: None of the five viewport steps derive from an app root — Tailwind's own untouched literals. The real trap sits one level up: globals.css's --container-app-* block LOOKS like it derives from the viewport scale (same px numbers) but is actually its own independently hand-set @theme declaration that has to be kept in sync by hand if the viewport scale ever changes.
collidingTokens: @app-lg: (container, pinned to the same 1024px — carries the 'shell column' meaning)
@lg: (Tailwind's own built-in container default, 512px — same lookalike name, half the pixel value, a different and already-live use case)
forbidden: typing bare @sm:/@md:/@lg:/@xl: when the intent is the shell-relative breakpoint — compiles clean, silently applies at half the intended pixel width
using plain viewport sm:/md:/lg:/xl: on something that lives inside the app shell column — looks correct until the content-AI rail actually narrows the shell
inventing an arbitrary breakpoint (min-[900px]) when one of the five already fits
readBy: layout/shell decision sheets — rail behavior, sidebar collapse, tab-label hide/show
entries.verifiedAgainst: node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css (--breakpoint-sm/md/lg/xl/2xl AND --container-sm/md/lg/xl defaults); D:/Repositories/starci-academy/src/app/globals.css (@theme --container-app-sm/md/lg/xl block and its explicit lg:→@lg: rename-trap comment); src/hooks/reuseables/useSmViewpoint.ts; grepped @sm:/@md:/@lg:/@xl:/@app-sm:/@app-md:/@app-lg: usage across GroupPressableCard, LessonPager, TalentDirectory, TabsCard, ResponsiveBreadcrumb, SettingsLayout, LearningHistory/CourseDetail, LearnMobileBar, LearnMobileTabBar

entries.name: z-index
entries.role: The stacking-order ladder for anything that must float above ordinary page flow; picks which literal z-* a block reaches for by role. Does not decide whether a block should float at all.

scale.use: chrome floating LOCALLY inside one component (mini-popover reaction bar, overlay button on article text) / -z-10 for decor placed BEHIND content (ambient background)
a control floating over an already-sticky region (rail resize-handle, video controls overlay)
sticky sub-header / in-page overlay, mostly mobile (filter bar, settings tab-strip, search-result dropdown, bottom sheet)
page-level chrome (FAB, sticky bottom bar, mobile bottom tab-bar, sticky filter row)

the navbar — the anchor use; also reached today by unrelated floating elements (contribution-calendar tooltip, diagram node popover, full-screen confetti) with no documented reason to sit exactly here rather than z-40
TopLoader (SPA nav progress bar) — must beat the navbar
highest live step: AppSplash (cold-load overlay) and ContentAiSelectionAsk — anything that must beat every other layer of chrome

entries.relation: Each step is an independent decision, not a formula — but every new z-index must anchor to the nearest existing step below, never a number in between (z-[45]) or an arbitrary high leap. If two overlays fight, the fix is architecture (render in-panel instead of a separate Modal/Drawer body), not a higher number.
notDerived: z-[1] in AIProcessingText's inner panel looks like it might be a step on this ladder but isn't — it's a purely local hack lifting one element above a z-auto sibling inside one small component, unrelated to the global 7-step scale.
collidingTokens: z-50 (navbar, the anchor use) vs z-50 (contribution-calendar tooltip, KnowledgeGraph ConceptNode popover, Confetti full-screen overlay — unrelated elements riding the same number opportunistically rather than by documented need)
forbidden: picking a z-index between two documented steps (z-[45]) or jumping to an arbitrary high value 'to be safe'
trying to win a z-fight against a popover-spawned overlay by raising the number instead of rendering in-panel
